statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-113408 is tracked in GitLab work item https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/git/-/work_items/809 . A server using Git protocol v2 can advertise an unborn HEAD whose symref target contains path-traversal characters, such as refs/heads/../../../TARGET. The client copied it into .git/HEAD without validation, and with the files ref backend later ref updates could write to unintended files. Upstream fixed it in Git 2.50.2, 2.51.3, 2.52.1, 2.53.1, 2.54.1, 2.55.1 and 2.56.1, as the Git 2.50.2 release notes describe: https://github.com/git/git/blob/v2.50.2/Documentation/RelNotes/2.50.2.adoc . The fix is three commits that run check_refname_format() in connect.c on the unborn HEAD symref target, the born HEAD symref target and every ref name in the ls-refs response, ignoring invalid values with a warning, and that check the unborn HEAD target again in builtin/clone.c: https://github.com/git/git/commit/b371db812524aa7831d3c3a9aed782defd1dcfb2 , https://github.com/git/git/commit/8cb7e2e031978c59381adf086fd1c0ce1e3a7315 and https://github.com/git/git/commit/f357b9c2c77eae1a1d37dfa44c1dda53f532a82a . The 2.52.1-r0 build is Alpine's security upgrade to Git 2.52.1: https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/commit/2f20de3527863b1b84f620fefe687921498e7240 . We checked /usr/bin/git, the program in the git package that contains the protocol v2 client code, in both published builds on x86_64 and aarch64. In 2.52.1-r0 it contains the fix's warning strings "remote advertised invalid symref-target" and "remote advertised invalid ref name". In 2.52.0-r0 it contains neither, although both builds contain the protocol's "symref-target:" string. Earlier builds of this owner predate the fix.

CVE-2026-113408 is tracked in GitLab work item https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/git/-/work_items/809 . A server using Git protocol v2 can advertise an unborn HEAD whose symref target contains path-traversal characters, such as refs/heads/../../../TARGET. The client copied it into .git/HEAD without validation, and with the files ref backend later ref updates could write to unintended files. Upstream fixed it in Git 2.50.2 and later maintenance releases, as the Git 2.50.2 release notes describe: https://github.com/git/git/blob/v2.50.2/Documentation/RelNotes/2.50.2.adoc . Debian's git 1:2.47.3-0+deb13u1 does not include the fix, and the Debian tracker still lists trixie as vulnerable: https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-113408 . DHI backports the three upstream commits, which run check_refname_format() in connect.c on the unborn HEAD symref target, the born HEAD symref target and every ref name in the ls-refs response, ignoring invalid values with a warning, and check the unborn HEAD target again in builtin/clone.c: https://github.com/git/git/commit/b371db812524aa7831d3c3a9aed782defd1dcfb2 , https://github.com/git/git/commit/8cb7e2e031978c59381adf086fd1c0ce1e3a7315 and https://github.com/git/git/commit/f357b9c2c77eae1a1d37dfa44c1dda53f532a82a . The fixed version is the first build that carries them, and its shipped changelog lists the CVE-2026-113408 backport. We checked all 13 ELF programs in the git package of the two builds in the DHI Debian repository, on amd64 and arm64, including /usr/bin/git and /usr/lib/git-core/git-remote-http. In the fixed build every one contains the fix's warning strings "remote advertised invalid symref-target" and "remote advertised invalid ref name". In the build before it none does, although every program in both builds contains the protocol's "symref-target:" string. Earlier builds of 2.47.3-0+deb13u1 also predate the backport.
